items.response: That error fits your OrbStack switch: compose is still trying the Docker Desktop socket under ~/.docker/run/docker.sock. I'd check which docker context or DOCKER_HOST it is using before changing anything. Action: run `docker context ls` and `echo $DOCKER_HOST`, switch to the OrbStack context (or unset the stale DOCKER_HOST), then retry `docker compose up`.

Glad it works. The web unit tests I started are still the open item, since they tell us whether any snapshot depended on the old sort order. Action: check the background test results and report back, fixing any snapshot that assumed oldest-first.

Understood, formatting only with zero logic changes. I don't know which formatter this repo uses, so I'll find its config first and use that instead of hand-editing. Action: find the repo's formatter/lint config, run it on apps/api/src/routes/payments.ts only, review the diff to confirm it is whitespace, quotes and semicolons only, then run the payments tests.

There is a real difference, not just style. structuredClone keeps Dates as Dates, plus Map, Set, typed arrays, undefined and circular references. The JSON round trip turns Dates into strings, drops undefined and functions, and throws on cycles. Neither copies class prototypes or functions (structuredClone throws on functions), and structuredClone is available on Node 18, so it is safe for your setup. Action: wait for the two background Node-compatibility checks to finish and report their results.

Plan: a worker job that loads the paid invoice and its org, skips if orgs.callback_url is empty, POSTs an invoice.paid JSON event with a timeout, and throws on non-2xx so the queue retries. I don't know the event payload shape, whether you want request signing, or where invoice-paid is currently emitted. Action: read the worker's existing jobs and queue setup, the schema for orgs.callback_url and the payment-succeeded code path, then implement the job with tests for missing URL, non-2xx and timeout.

Will do: fix the reports empty state copy and sweep for the same misspelling elsewhere. I'll make the search case-insensitive and cover variants like recieved and recieving, not just recieve. Action: grep the whole repo (excluding node_modules and lockfiles) for the typo, fix each hit, and list what changed so you can see if any are in strings that tests assert on.

I'll point kubectl at the prod cluster (acme-prod on EKS) and look at the worker pods. I can't tell who gets woken up from here, since I have no notes on the on-call rotation, so I won't guess a name. Action: run `aws eks update-kubeconfig --name acme-prod --region us-east-1`, then `kubectl get pods` for the worker (checking the namespace first), `describe` a crashing pod and read `logs --previous`; for who is paged I'll look for the escalation policy in the runbooks or the paging tool, or you can tell me.

I'll scaffold it next to the clients command with --json support, and treat that as the rule for every command from now on. My notes say the CLI moved from yargs to commander (each group exports a registerX(program)), and that public CLI changes belong in docs/cli.md. They also hint an invoices list may already exist, so I'll check before creating a duplicate. Action: look at packages/cli/src/commands (clients and any existing invoices), add or extend `invoices list` hitting GET /v1/invoices with a table plus --json, register it, add a vitest test, and update docs/cli.md.

Sounds like the export handler never clears its loading state when there is nothing to export, so I'd start there. I haven't looked at the code yet, so I won't claim the exact cause. Action: reproduce with an org that has zero invoices, read the export button handler and the endpoint's empty-result response, fix the loading reset (and show a sensible empty message), and add a test for the zero-invoice case.

That is a separate concern from the render-fallback work, so I'd keep it off acme-447 unless you say otherwise. The sturdiest way to make filters survive back navigation is to keep them in the URL search params instead of component state. Action: read how the invoice list holds status, client and date-range state now, move it to URL query params (with the existing router utilities), and test that back navigation restores the filters.
Yes, fine. It has been built in since Node 17, and your pinned version (20.11) is well past that.

I'll add tests for the from/to filtering on the invoices route: both bounds, only from, only to, boundary dates inclusive, and invalid input. I need to check what the route does for a bad or reversed range so the tests assert real behavior. Action: read the existing route tests, add those cases, run coverage to confirm it stays at or above 80% lines, then reply with a short bullet summary, not paragraphs.

Plan: a daily repeatable job per org that finds invoices due in exactly 3 days and enqueues one reminder email job per invoice, with a deterministic job id so reruns can't double-send. For the email I'd use the subject format from your earlier note: Reminder: INV-2026-0412 is due in 3 days (with the real invoice number). Which timezone defines due in 3 days for an org is something I'll check in the schema instead of assuming. Action: read the worker's existing queue setup and invoice schema, then add the invoice-reminders queue, scheduler and enqueue logic with tests.

structuredClone handles more types correctly: Dates stay Dates, Map, Set, typed arrays, undefined and circular references survive. JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x)) turns Dates into strings, drops undefined and functions, and throws on cycles. Neither copies class prototypes, and structuredClone throws on functions where JSON silently drops them. Action: none needed; happy to look at a specific spot in the code if you want to switch one.

Got it, apps/api/src/routes/v1/payments.ts stays as is, with the 'recieved' response value untouched. The worker spelling fixes stand. Action: wait for the api tests to finish, confirm they match the worker-only change, and note the response value as a possible API cleanup for later.

On it. I'll search both directories for the misspelling and fix it where it is a comment, log message or string only a human reads. If any hit is a value clients or tests could compare against, such as a response field, I'll flag it instead of silently changing it. Action: grep -rn 'recieved' in apps/api and services/worker, fix the safe ones, then run both packages' tests.

A timeout in beforeAll usually means the setup step never finishes, such as a database or container that isn't reachable, but I won't guess before seeing the output. Action: run the orders route tests, read the first error and where beforeAll hangs, check what the setup depends on (database, containers, env vars) and whether it is running on your machine, then fix the cause rather than just raising the timeout.

The debounce is a different concern, so I'd put it in a separate commit, and ideally a separate branch, unless you want it on the CLI branch. Action: git status to confirm exactly those 4 files, commit them with a clear message, then find the dashboard invoice search input and debounce its request by about 300ms with a test.

You're welcome. The worker typo fixes are in, the api one is left alone on purpose, and the api suite passed (318 tests, payments.test.ts still expects 'recieved'). Action: nothing pending; I'll note the payments status value as a possible API cleanup for later.

Ha, not bored exactly, though I'll admit renames are about as mechanical as it gets. At least this one was clean: typecheck passed with 0 errors and nothing references the old name. Action: nothing needed, enjoy the end of the week; ping me if you want anything else queued up.

I'll build the duplicate button with the shadcn Button from apps/web/components/ui and a lucide-react icon, not our hand-rolled icons. Since it is icon-only, it gets an aria-label (like 'Duplicate line item' plus the description) and the icon is aria-hidden, per your accessibility rule. Action: open the line item row, add the button next to the trash one with a duplicate handler, add a test, and then do the broader icon-only-button sweep after this.

Next attaches a digest to errors it passes to global-error, and Sentry won't pick that up by itself, so the capture probably needs it added explicitly. I haven't opened the file yet, so I'll confirm how the event is captured before changing it. Action: read app/global-error.tsx, add the error digest as a Sentry tag (searchable) and extra data when present, add a test if the file is testable, and avoid logging anything beyond the digest.

For CORS, I'll make the api allow only origins listed in CORS_ORIGINS (comma separated), and nothing else. Action: look at the PR diff and git log for when .eslintrc.json and .prettierrc were removed, then change the api CORS config to parse and trim the env var and reject every other origin (an empty or missing var allows none), with tests.

I'll add a delete button on the customer detail page with a confirm dialog, using the shadcn AlertDialog and the existing components. It calls DELETE /v1/customers/:id, which does a soft delete, and on failure it shows the title from the problem+json error body and keeps the dialog open. The api route is still not registered in app.ts, so I'll wire that up too. Action: read the detail page and current UI patterns, add the button, a server action and a test, then register the route and run the checks.

Will do: the customer delete returns a 409 when open invoices exist, built with the existing problem() helper so it is problem+json like every other error. What counts as open is something I'll read from the schema rather than assume, and I'll use the same type URI convention the helper already uses. Action: add the open-invoices check before the soft delete in the DELETE handler, return problem() with status 409, and add a test for the 409 body and content type.

Sounds good, I'll leave the social login check with you and add the video now. I'll use a YouTube iframe with id aB3xK9qLm2Q inside a 16:9 wrapper that scales to the container width.
